text.p: Here highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The leader of the nationalist rightwing Confederation for Independent Poland (KPN) Leszek Moczulski has left the Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS) group with plans to start a rightist elections committee not dominated by trade unions.
- AWS leader Marian Krzaklewski wants to change the 1998 budget so as to limit central redistribution and increase the revenues of local communities and municipalities.
- Poland's current floods may bring about losses similar to those suffered in 1996 when they reached 422 million zlotys, the country's flood prevention committee secretary Ryszard Egler said.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET NEWS RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The number of Poland's mobile telecoms subscribers grew by 48,900 in May 1997 to 6.772 million, showing a 14 percent upturn compared with the same time last year, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.

- The Lech Browary Wielkopolskie (LBW) breweries has joined the British Chamber of Commerce which includes 250 British, Polish and international firms operating in Poland, the LBW's spokesman Piotr Jurjewicz said.

- The Fama Gniew shipping engineering plant has received the International Standards Organisation (ISO)-9001 quality certificate awarded by the Germanischer Lloyd Certification Hamburg and the Polish Shipping Regisrter in Gdansk.

- The Warsaw economic court has registered the Naftobazy oil tank centres' administration firm on July 1, 1997. Previously the tank operator was a subsidiary of the state-owned CPN fuel processor and distributor.
- A group of 200 small business retailers have formed a joint stock company to build a 42,000 square metre trade centre in south Warsaw,

- Poland's breweries produced 16.5 million hectolitres of beer in 1996 showing a 7.1 percent increase compared with the year before. Domestic breweries invested over 400 million zlotys in development last year.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
- The Huta Sedzimira steel mill plans to issue Eurobonds and restructure its debts this autumn. The plant will choose a privatisation advisor by the end of July.
- Poland's national flag Carrier PLL LOT and the American Airlines have increased the number of weekly code-share flights between Poland and selected cities in the US to 26 connections, LOT said.
- The Atlas construction glue maker has a 75 market share in the domestic market and the firm's sales will exceed 310 million zlotys in 1997, Atlas' marketing deputy director Roman Rojek said.
- The ZM Kolo meat processing plant will up share capital to 36.5 million zlotys through an issue of 450,000 shares nominally worth 10 zlotys per share, the company's shareholders decided.

- The Pollena EWA cosmetics maker in Lodz, central Poland, will produce a share issue prospectus to be presented to the Polish Securities Commission in the third quarter of 1997, Pollena's official Jacek Wolski said.
PARKIET
- The Polish Scientific Publishers (PWN) will shortly change into a joint stock company and prepare for a share listing on the Warsaw bourse next year, PWN's financial director Leszek Gawkowski said.
- The Pekao SA group earned a net profit of 284.3 million zlotys first five months of 1997 which exceeded the results in of the first half of last year, the group said.
NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
